title: Trump Addresses Dayton and El Paso Shootings in August 5 Remarks
description_short: On August 5, 2019, Trump addressed the Dayton and El Paso attacks, expressed sympathy for victims and survivors, and said he directed federal authorities to help.
description_medium: On August 5, 2019, President Donald Trump delivered White House remarks about the attacks in Dayton, Ohio, and El Paso, Texas. He said nine people were killed and 27 injured in Dayton, expressed sympathy for victims, families, and survivors, and said he had spoken with Ohio Governor Mike DeWine and Dayton Mayor Nan Whaley. Trump also said he directed federal authorities to provide any assistance required.
description_long: At 10:08 a.m. on August 5, 2019, President Donald Trump spoke in the White House Diplomatic Reception Room about the attacks in El Paso, Texas, and Dayton, Ohio. In describing Dayton, he said nine people had been killed, including the gunman’s sister, and 27 injured; these casualty figures are attributed to Trump’s remarks. He and the First Lady joined Americans in mourning victims, their families, and survivors. Trump said he had spoken with Ohio Governor Mike DeWine and Dayton Mayor Nan Whaley to express sadness and support. He also said he was in close contact with Attorney General William Barr and FBI Director Christopher Wray. Trump stated that he had directed federal authorities to provide any assistance required. The transcript documents his public response to the two attacks and the assistance directive he announced. This is the August 5 statement, distinct from the August 4 Dayton shooting itself. It does not assert that Trump caused the attack or that his response changed the investigation or the outcome.
